correctness.rationale: For all complete multipartite K_(n1,...,nr) with r>=3, the vertex-weighted Matrix–Tree determinant yields F(z)=(prod z_v) Z^(r-2) prod_p(Z-Z_p)^(n_p-1). Normalization gives independent categorical occupancy draws for X_v=D_v-1. Direct conditioning on each draw establishes Cov(X_u,1[X_v=0])=q_v W_uv for u!=v; the same-vertex contribution is -q_u E[X_u] and E[X_u]=sum_(v!=u) W_uv. Hence the claimed weighted-Laplacian identity follows without independence of vertex degrees. All W_uv>0 for r>=3, while q_p increases strictly with n_p because (1-1/(N-s))^(s-1) decreases in s. Thus smallest and largest part signs follow for unequal sizes; equal parts give zero. Separate r=2 generating-function factorization proves every bipartite covariance zero, including stars. The explicit intermediate-part signs for K_(1,2,3) and K_(1,2,4) are -11/1296 and 32/2205. An independent exact-rational calculation reproduces these. The inspected Prüfer-code verifier covers eight families up to seven vertices and is not a proof of unrestricted sizes.

value.rationale: Total leaves and a marked vertex degree are canonical uniform-spanning-tree observables. Their dependence is not fixed-sign: smallest and largest multipartition classes have opposite signs, every bipartite graph has zero despite imbalance, and intermediate classes switch sign in small exact examples. The structural weighted-Laplacian law simultaneously explains these phenomena and supplies a reusable exact covariance calculation rather than a textbook substitution.
